   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:InvestmentPolicyTextBlock" id="c141183760" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;"><b><i>Investments</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Investments are recorded at fair value. Pursuant to the amended SEC Rule <em style="font: inherit;">2a</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">5</em> of the <em style="font: inherit;">1940</em> Act, on <em style="font: inherit;"> July 29, 2022, </em>the Board&#160;designated the Advisor as the Company&#8217;s &#8220;valuation designee.&#8221; The valuation designee determines the fair value of the Company&#8217;s portfolio investments and the Company's Board oversees the valuation designee. The Company has the intent to hold its debt investments for the foreseeable future or until maturity or payoff.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Interest on debt investments is accrued and included in income based on contractual rates applied to principal amounts outstanding. Interest income is determined using a method that results in a level rate of return on principal amounts outstanding. Generally, when a debt investment becomes <em style="font: inherit;">90</em>&#160;days or more past due, or if the Company otherwise does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> expect to receive interest and principal repayments, the debt investment is placed on non-accrual status and the recognition of interest income <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be discontinued. Interest payments received on non-accrual debt investments <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be recognized as income, on a cash basis, or applied to principal depending upon management&#8217;s judgment at the time the debt investment is placed on non-accrual status. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, there were <em style="font: inherit;">three</em>&#160;investments on non-accrual status with a cost of $<ix:nonFraction id="c141178823" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_InvestmentTypeAxis-FourInvestmentsMember" unitRef="USD" name="hrzn:InvestmentsCostNonaccrualStatus" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">32.8</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and a fair value of $<ix:nonFraction id="c141178824" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_InvestmentTypeAxis-FourInvestmentsMember" unitRef="USD" name="hrzn:InvestmentsFairValueNonaccrualStatus" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">24.5</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024</em>, there were <em style="font: inherit;">four</em>&#160;investments on non-accrual status with a cost of $<ix:nonFraction id="c141178826" contextRef="i_2024-12-31_InvestmentTypeAxis-FourInvestmentsMember" unitRef="USD" name="hrzn:InvestmentsCostNonaccrualStatus" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">44.8</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and a fair value of $<ix:nonFraction id="c141178827" contextRef="i_2024-12-31_InvestmentTypeAxis-FourInvestmentsMember" unitRef="USD" name="hrzn:InvestmentsFairValueNonaccrualStatus" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">10.5</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million. For the&#160;year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, the Company recognized&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c141178829" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="hrzn:InvestmentsNonaccrualInterestIncome" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.3</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c141178830" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="hrzn:InvestmentsNonaccrualInterestIncome" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.2</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, respectively,&#160;received from debt investments while on non-accrual status. For the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31,&#160;</em><em style="font: inherit;">2023,</em> the Company did <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c141178832">not</span> recognize any interest income from debt investments while on non-accrual status. &#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -2pt; text-indent: 18pt;">From time to time, the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>have debt investments&#160;that contain a PIK provision. Contractual PIK interest, which represents contractually deferred interest added to the loan balance that is generally due at the end of the loan term, is generally recorded on an accrual basis to the extent such amounts are expected to be collected. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, there were <em style="font: inherit;">six</em> and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">five</em> investments, respectively,&#160;with PIK provisions.&#160;For the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em><em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>&#160;PIK interest income totaled $<ix:nonFraction id="c141178838" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:InterestIncomeOperatingPaidInKind" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">2.3</ix:nonFraction> million, $<ix:nonFraction id="c141178839" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:InterestIncomeOperatingPaidInKind" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">3.3</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c141178840" contextRef="d_2023-01-01_2023-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:InterestIncomeOperatingPaidInKind" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">8.4</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, respectively. For the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em><em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>, <ix:nonFraction id="c141178843" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="hrzn:InvestmentIncomeAttributableToNoncashPaidinkindInterestPercent" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">2.4</ix:nonFraction>%, <ix:nonFraction id="c141178844" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="hrzn:InvestmentIncomeAttributableToNoncashPaidinkindInterestPercent" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">3.3</ix:nonFraction>%, and <ix:nonFraction id="c141178845" contextRef="d_2023-01-01_2023-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="hrzn:InvestmentIncomeAttributableToNoncashPaidinkindInterestPercent" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">7.4</ix:nonFraction>%&#160;of the Company&#8217;s total investment income was attributable to non-cash PIK interest income, respectively. The Company will generally cease accruing PIK interest if management does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> expect the portfolio company to be able to pay all principal and interest due. For the&#160;year&#160;ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2023</em>, <em style="font: inherit;">two</em>&#160;debt investments, which had accrued PIK interest into income of $<ix:nonFraction id="c141178852" contextRef="d_2023-01-01_2023-12-31_InvestmentTypeAxis-TwoInvestmentsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:InterestIncomeOperatingPaidInKind" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">3.9</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million during the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2023</em>&#160;was placed on nonaccrual status.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The Company receives a variety of fees from borrowers in the ordinary course of conducting its business, including advisory fees, commitment fees, amendment fees, non-utilization fees, success fees and prepayment fees. In a limited number of cases, the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>also receive a non-refundable deposit earned upon the termination of a transaction. Debt investment origination fees, net of certain direct origination costs, are deferred and, along with unearned income, are amortized as a level-yield adjustment over the respective term of the debt investment. All other income is recognized when earned. Fees for counterparty debt investment commitments with multiple debt investments are allocated to each debt investment based upon each debt investment&#8217;s relative fair value. When a debt investment is placed on non-accrual status, the amortization of the related fees and unearned income is discontinued until the debt investment is returned to accrual status.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Certain debt investment agreements also require the borrower to make an ETP, that is accrued into interest receivable and taken into income over the life of the debt investment to the extent such amounts are expected to be collected. The Company will generally cease accruing the income if there is insufficient value to support the accrual or the Company does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> expect the borrower to be able to pay the ETP when due. The proportion of the Company&#8217;s total investment income that resulted from the portion of ETPs <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> received in cash for the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em><em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em> was <ix:nonFraction id="c141178857" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="hrzn:InvestmentNonaccrualIncomeNotReceivedInCashPercent" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">3.9</ix:nonFraction>%, <ix:nonFraction id="c141178858" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="hrzn:InvestmentNonaccrualIncomeNotReceivedInCashPercent" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">5.6</ix:nonFraction>% and <ix:nonFraction id="c141178859" contextRef="d_2023-01-01_2023-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="hrzn:InvestmentNonaccrualIncomeNotReceivedInCashPercent" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">4.2</ix:nonFraction>%, respectively.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">In connection with substantially all lending arrangements, the Company receives warrants to purchase shares of stock from the borrower. The warrants are recorded as assets at estimated fair value on the grant date using the Black-Scholes valuation model. The warrants are considered loan fees and are recorded as unearned income on the grant date. The unearned income is recognized as interest income over the contractual life of the related debt investment in accordance with the Company&#8217;s income recognition policy. Subsequent to debt investment origination, the fair value of the warrants is determined using the Black-Scholes valuation model. Any adjustment to fair value is recorded through earnings as net unrealized appreciation or depreciation on investments. Gains and losses from the disposition of the warrants or stock acquired from the exercise of warrants are recognized as realized gains and losses on investments.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Realized gains or losses on the sale of investments, or upon the determination that an investment balance, or portion thereof, is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> recoverable, are calculated using the specific identification method. The Company measures realized gains or losses by calculating the difference between the net proceeds from the repayment or sale and the amortized cost basis of the investment. Net unrealized appreciation or depreciation reflects the change in the fair values of the Company&#8217;s portfolio investments during the reporting period, including any reversal of previously recorded unrealized appreciation or depreciation when gains or losses are realized.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:DebtPolicyTextBlock" id="c141183761" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;"><b><i>Debt issuance costs</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Debt issuance costs are fees and other direct incremental costs incurred by the Company in obtaining debt financing from its lenders and issuing debt securities. The unamortized balance of debt issuance costs as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> was $<ix:nonFraction id="c141178863" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredFinanceCostsNet" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">10.6</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c141178864" contextRef="i_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredFinanceCostsNet" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">8.9</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, respectively. These amounts are capitalized and amortized and included in interest expense in the consolidated statements of operations over the life of the borrowings. The accumulated amortization balances as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> were $<ix:nonFraction id="c141178866" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AccumulatedAmortizationDeferredFinanceCosts" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">8.9</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c141178867" contextRef="i_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AccumulatedAmortizationDeferredFinanceCosts" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">7.2</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, respectively. The amortization expense for the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em><em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em> was $<ix:nonFraction id="c141178870" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AmortizationOfFinancingCosts" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">2.6</ix:nonFraction> million, $<ix:nonFraction id="c141178871" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AmortizationOfFinancingCosts" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.8</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c141178872" contextRef="d_2023-01-01_2023-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AmortizationOfFinancingCosts" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.9</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, respectively.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxPolicyTextBlock" id="c141183762" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;"><b><i>Income taxes</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">As a BDC, the Company has elected to be treated as a RIC under Subchapter M of the Code and operates in a manner so as to qualify for the tax treatment applicable to RICs. In order to qualify as a RIC and to avoid the imposition of corporate-level income tax on the portion of its taxable income distributed to stockholders, among other things, the Company is required to meet certain source-of-income and asset diversification requirements and to timely distribute dividends out of assets legally available for distribution to its stockholders of an amount generally at least equal to <em style="font: inherit;">90%</em> of its investment company taxable income, as defined by the Code and determined without regard to any deduction for dividends paid, for each tax&#160;year. The Company, among other things, has made and intends to continue to make the requisite distributions to its stockholders, which generally relieves the Company from corporate-level U.S. federal income taxes. Accordingly, <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> provision for federal income tax has been recorded in the financial statements. Differences between taxable income and net increase in net assets resulting from operations either can be temporary, meaning they will reverse in the future, or permanent. In accordance with ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">946,</em> <i>Financial Services</i>&#8212;<i>Investment Companies</i>, as amended, of the Financial Accounting Standards Board&#160;(&#8220;FASB&#8221;), permanent tax differences, such as non-deductible excise taxes paid, are reclassified from distributions in excess of net investment income and net realized loss on investments to paid-in-capital at the end of each fiscal&#160;year. These permanent book-to-tax differences are reclassified on the consolidated statements of changes in net assets to reflect their tax character but have <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> impact on total net assets. For the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em><em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>, the Company reclassified $<ix:nonFraction id="c141178879" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ExciseAndSalesTaxes" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, $<ix:nonFraction id="c141178880" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="hrzn:AdjustmentsToAdditionalPaidInCapitalNondeductibleExciseTaxesPaid" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.5</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c141178881" contextRef="d_2023-01-01_2023-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="hrzn:AdjustmentsToAdditionalPaidInCapitalNondeductibleExciseTaxesPaid" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.5</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, respectively, to paid-in capital from distributions in excess of net investment income, which related to excise taxes payable.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Depending on the level of taxable income earned in a tax&#160;year, the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>choose to carry forward taxable income in excess of current&#160;year distributions into the next tax&#160;year and incur a <ix:nonFraction id="c141178882" contextRef="i_2024-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="hrzn:FederalExciseTaxPercent" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">4</ix:nonFraction>% U.S. federal excise tax on such income, as required. To the extent that the Company determines that its estimated current&#160;year annual taxable income will be in excess of estimated current&#160;year distributions, the Company accrues excise tax, if any, on estimated excess taxable income as taxable income is earned. For the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em><em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>, $<ix:nonFraction id="c141178885" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ExciseAndSalesTaxes" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, $<ix:nonFraction id="c141178886" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ExciseAndSalesTaxes" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.5</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c141178887" contextRef="d_2023-01-01_2023-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ExciseAndSalesTaxes" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.5</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, respectively, was accrued for U.S. federal excise tax.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The Company evaluates tax positions taken in the course of preparing the Company&#8217;s tax returns to determine whether the tax positions are &#8220;more-likely-than-<em style="font: inherit;">not&#8221;</em> to be sustained by the applicable tax authority in accordance with ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">740,</em> <i>Income Taxes</i>, as modified by ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">946.</em> Tax benefits of positions <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> deemed to meet the more-likely-than-<em style="font: inherit;">not</em> threshold, or uncertain tax positions, would be recorded as a tax expense in the current&#160;year. It is the Company&#8217;s policy to recognize accrued interest and penalties related to uncertain tax benefits in income tax expense. The Company had <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c141178893"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c141179979">no</span></span> material uncertain tax positions at <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>. The Company&#8217;s income tax returns for the <em style="font: inherit;">2025,</em> <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c141178896">2024,</span> <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>&#160;and <em style="font: inherit;">2022</em>&#160;tax&#160;years remain subject to examination by U.S. federal and state tax authorities.</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Distributions to common stockholders are recorded on the declaration date. The Board continually monitors and reassesses the amount of cash&#160;to be paid out as distributions relative to the net investment income generated by the Company and other metrics. Net realized capital gains, if any, <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be distributed, although the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>decide to retain such net realized gains for investment.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The Company has adopted a dividend reinvestment plan that provides for reinvestment of cash distributions on behalf of its stockholders, unless a stockholder elects to receive cash. As a result, if the Board declares a cash distribution, then stockholders who have <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> &#8220;opted out&#8221; of the dividend reinvestment plan will have their cash distributions automatically reinvested in additional shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock, rather than receiving the cash distribution. The Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>issue new shares or purchase shares in the open market to fulfill its obligations under the plan.</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">During the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2023</em>, the Company sold <ix:nonFraction id="c141178919" contextRef="d_2023-01-01_2023-12-31_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-The2023And2021EquityDistributionAgreementsMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesNewIssues" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">2,248,830</ix:nonFraction> shares of common stock under the <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em> Equity Distribution Agreement and the <em style="font: inherit;">2021</em> Equity Distribution Agreement. For the same period, the Company received total accumulated net proceeds of approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c141178922" contextRef="d_2023-01-01_2023-12-31_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-The2023And2021EquityDistributionAgreementsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ProceedsFromIssuanceOfCommonStock" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">26.2</ix:nonFraction> million, including $<ix:nonFraction id="c141178923" contextRef="d_2023-01-01_2023-12-31_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-The2023And2021EquityDistributionAgreementsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:PaymentsOfStockIssuanceCosts" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.7</ix:nonFraction> million of offering expenses, from these sales.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The Company generally uses net proceeds from these offerings to make investments, to pay down liabilities and for general corporate purposes. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, shares representing approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c141178924" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-The2023EquityDistributionAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="hrzn:EquitySalesAgreementRemainingAmountAvailableForIssuance" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">64.3</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million of its common stock remain available for issuance and sale under the <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em> Equity Distribution Agreement.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">On&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 2, 2023,&#160;</em>the Company completed a follow-on public offering of&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c141178927" contextRef="d_2023-06-02_2023-06-02_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-PublicOfferingMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesNewIssues" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">3,250,000</ix:nonFraction>&#160;shares of its common stock at a public offering price of $<ix:nonFraction id="c141178928" contextRef="i_2023-06-02_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-PublicOfferingMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:SharesIssuedPricePerShare" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">12.50</ix:nonFraction>&#160;per share, for total net proceeds to the Company of $<ix:nonFraction id="c141178929" contextRef="d_2023-06-02_2023-06-02_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-PublicOfferingMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ProceedsFromIssuanceOfCommonStock" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">38.9</ix:nonFraction> million, after deducting underwriting commission and discounts and other offering expenses.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="hrzn:StockRepurchaseProgramPolicyTextBlock" id="c141183765" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;"><b><i>Stock Repurchase Program</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> April&#160;</em><em style="font: inherit;">25,</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2025,</em> the Board extended a previously authorized stock repurchase program which allows the Company to repurchase up to $<ix:nonFraction id="c141178932" contextRef="i_2024-04-26" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:StockRepurchaseProgramRemainingAuthorizedRepurchaseAmount1" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">5.0</ix:nonFraction> million of its common stock at prices below the Company&#8217;s net asset value per share as reported in its most recent consolidated financial statements. Under the repurchase program, the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may, </em>but is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> obligated to, repurchase shares of its outstanding common stock in the open market or in privately negotiated transactions from time to time. Any repurchases by the Company intends to&#160;comply with the requirements of Rule&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">10b&#8209;18</em> under the Securities Exchange Act of <em style="font: inherit;">1934,</em> as amended (the &#8220;Exchange Act&#8221;), and any applicable requirements of the <em style="font: inherit;">1940</em> Act. Unless extended by the Board, the repurchase program will terminate on the earlier of <em style="font: inherit;"> June&#160;</em><em style="font: inherit;">30,</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em>&#160;or the repurchase of <em style="font: inherit;">$5.0</em> million of the Company&#8217;s common stock. On <em style="font: inherit;"> August 5, 2025, </em>the Board&#160;authorized an increase in the maximum amount of shares of the Company that can be repurchased on the open market or in privately negotiated purchases pursuant to Rule <em style="font: inherit;">10b</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">18</em> and other applicable provisions of the Securities Exchange Act of <em style="font: inherit;">1934,</em> as amended from up to <em style="font: inherit;">$5,000,000</em> of shares to up to $<ix:nonFraction id="c141178944" contextRef="i_2025-08-05" unitRef="USD" name="srt:StockRepurchaseProgramAuthorizedAmount1" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">10,000,000</ix:nonFraction> of shares, provided such purchases, in the aggregate, do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> exceed <em style="font: inherit;">two</em> percent (<ix:nonFraction id="c141178947" contextRef="i_2025-08-05" unitRef="Pure" name="hrzn:StockRepurchaseProgramPercentageOfOutstandingStockMaximum" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">2</ix:nonFraction>%) of the shares outstanding at the time of purchase and such shares are purchased only when the such shares are trading below <ix:nonFraction id="c141178948" contextRef="i_2025-08-05" unitRef="Pure" name="hrzn:StockRepurchaseProgramMaximumPercentageOfNetAssetValue" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="1">90</ix:nonFraction>% of the Company's most recently disclosed net asset value per share. During the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em><em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>, the Company did <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c141178951"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c141179980"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c141179981">not</span></span></span> make any repurchases of its common stock. From the inception of the stock repurchase program through <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, the Company repurchased <ix:nonFraction id="c141178952" contextRef="d_2021-04-24_2025-12-31" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:StockRepurchasedDuringPeriodShares" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">167,465</ix:nonFraction> shares of its common stock at an average price of $<ix:nonFraction id="c141178953" contextRef="d_2021-04-24_2025-12-31" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="hrzn:StockRepurchasedDuringPeriodPerShare" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">11.22</ix:nonFraction> on the open market at a total cost of $<ix:nonFraction id="c141178954" contextRef="d_2021-04-24_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:StockRepurchasedDuringPeriodValue" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.9</ix:nonFraction> million. From time to time, the Board assesses the size and effectiveness of the stock repurchase program and could elect to increase or decrease the size of the program in the future.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:TransfersAndServicingOfFinancialAssetsServicingOfFinancialAssetsPolicy" id="c141183766" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;"><b><i>Transfers of financial assets</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Assets related to transactions that do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> meet the requirements under ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">860,</em> <i>Transfers and Servicing </i>for sale treatment under GAAP are reflected in the Company&#8217;s consolidated statements of assets and liabilities as investments. Those assets are owned by special purpose entities that are consolidated in the Company&#8217;s financial statements. The creditors of the special purpose entities have received security interests in such assets and such assets are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> intended to be available to the creditors of the Company (or any other affiliate of the Company).</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Transfers of financial assets are accounted for as sales when control over the assets has been surrendered. Control over transferred assets is deemed to be surrendered when (<em style="font: inherit;">1</em>)&#160;the assets have been isolated from the Company&#160;&#8212; put presumptively beyond the reach of the transferor and its creditors, even in bankruptcy or other receivership, (<em style="font: inherit;">2</em>)&#160;the transferee obtains the right (free of conditions that constrain it from taking advantage of that right) to pledge or exchange the transferred assets and (<em style="font: inherit;">3</em>)&#160;the transferor does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> maintain effective control over the transferred assets through either (a)&#160;an agreement that both entitles and obligates the transferor to repurchase or redeem the assets before maturity or (b)&#160;the ability to unilaterally cause the holder to return specific assets, other than through a cleanup call.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-indent: 18pt;"><i><b></b></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c141183767" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-indent: 18pt;"><i><b>Recently issued&#160;accounting pronouncement</b></i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> November 2024, </em>the FASB issued Accounting Standards Update (&#8220;ASU&#8221;) <em style="font: inherit;">No.</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03,</em> Income Statement - Reporting Comprehensive Income - Expense Disaggregation Disclosures (Subtopic <em style="font: inherit;">220</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">40</em>). ASU <em style="font: inherit;">No.</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03</em> requires disaggregated disclosure of certain costs and expenses, including purchase of inventory, employee compensation, depreciation, amortization and depletion, within relevant income statement captions. ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03</em> is effective for years beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2026, </em>and interim periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2027. </em>Early adoption and retrospective application are permitted. The Company is currently evaluating the impact ASU <em style="font: inherit;">No.</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03.</em></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;"><em style="font: inherit;"></em></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Note</b>&#160;<b><em style="font: inherit;">3.</em></b>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;<b>Related party transactions</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;"><b><i>Investment Management Agreement</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -2pt; text-indent: 18pt;">At a meeting of the stockholders convened on&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> May 25, 2023&#160;</em>and reconvened on&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 28, 2023</em><i>,</i>&#160;the Company&#8217;s stockholders, upon the recommendation of the Board, approved an&#160;investment management agreement with the Advisor, which became effective on&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2023</em><i> </i>(the&#160;&#8220;Original Investment Management Agreement&#8221;).&#160;The Original Investment Management Agreement was&#160;effective for <em style="font: inherit;">two</em>&#160;years from the date of approval and then was required to&#160;be annually reapproved by the&#160;Board for a <em style="font: inherit;">one</em>-year period. The Original Investment Management Agreement was considered and reapproved by the Company&#8217;s Board, including a majority of the independent directors, on <em style="font: inherit;"> December 10, 2024 </em>for a <em style="font: inherit;">one</em>-year period.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -2pt; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2025, </em>the Company entered into a new investment management agreement with the Advisor (the &#8220;New Investment Management Agreement&#8221;, collectively with the Original Investment Management Agreement, the &#8220;Investment Management Agreement&#8221;) in connection with the closing of a transaction pursuant to which Momentum US Bidco LLC, an affiliate of Wendel SE, acquired <ix:nonFraction id="c141178980" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_LegalEntityAxis-MomentumUSBidcoLLCMember_OwnershipAxis-MonroeCapitalIntermediateHoldingsLLCMember_TypeOfArrangementAxis-EquityPurchaseAgreementMember" unitRef="Pure" name="hrzn:OwnershipPercentageAcquired" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">75</ix:nonFraction>% of the outstanding equity interests of Monroe Capital Intermediate Holdings, LLC, the indirect parent company of the Advisor, and certain other affiliates of Monroe Capital LLC (the &#8220;Transaction&#8221;) (any such affiliate party to the Transaction, collectively, &#8220;Monroe&#8221;). The Transaction, if closed, would constitute a change of control in the Advisor and terminated the Original Investment Management Agreement. On <em style="font: inherit;"> December 10, 2024, </em>the Company&#8217;s Board, including a majority of the independent directors, approved, and recommended for approval by the Company&#8217;s stockholders, the New Investment Management Agreement. The New Investment Management Agreement was approved, subject to the closing of the Transaction, by the Company&#8217;s stockholders at a special meeting of stockholders held on <em style="font: inherit;"> February 21, 2025. </em>The terms of the New Investment Management Agreement, including the fee structure and services to be provided, are the same as the terms of the Original Investment Management Agreement, except for the date and term. Under the terms of the Investment Management Agreement, the Advisor determines the composition of the Company&#8217;s investment portfolio, the nature and timing of the changes to the investment portfolio and the manner of implementing such changes; identifies, evaluates and negotiates the structure of the investments the Company makes (including performing due diligence on the Company&#8217;s prospective portfolio companies); and closes, monitors and administers the investments the Company makes, including the exercise of any voting or consent rights.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">The Advisor&#8217;s services under the Investment Management Agreement are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> exclusive to the Company, and the Advisor is free to furnish similar services to other entities so long as its services to the Company are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> impaired. The Advisor is a registered investment adviser with the SEC. The Advisor receives fees for providing services to the Company under the Investment Management Agreement, consisting of <em style="font: inherit;">two</em> components, a base management fee and an incentive fee.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The base management fee is calculated at an annual rate of <ix:nonFraction id="c141178985" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_TypeOfArrangementAxis-InvestmentManagementAgreementMember" unitRef="Pure" name="hrzn:BaseManagementFeeAnnualPercent" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">2.00</ix:nonFraction>% of the Company&#8217;s gross assets (less cash and cash equivalents) including any assets acquired with the proceeds of leverage; provided, that, to the extent the Company&#8217;s gross assets (less cash and cash equivalents) exceed <em style="font: inherit;">$250</em> million, the base management fee on the amount of such excess over <em style="font: inherit;">$250</em> million will be calculated at an annual rate of <ix:nonFraction id="c141178988" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_TypeOfArrangementAxis-InvestmentManagementAgreementMember" unitRef="Pure" name="hrzn:BaseManagementFeeAnnualPercentGrossAssetsExceeding250Million" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">1.60</ix:nonFraction>% of the Company&#8217;s gross assets (less cash and cash equivalents) including any assets acquired with the proceeds of leverage. The base management fee is payable&#160;monthly in arrears and is prorated for any partial&#160;month.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The base management fee payable at <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> was&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c141178990" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_TypeOfArrangementAxis-InvestmentManagementAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ManagementFeePayable" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">1.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million. The base management fee expense was $<ix:nonFraction id="c141178991" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_TypeOfArrangementAxis-InvestmentManagementAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ManagementFeeExpense" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">11.7</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, $<ix:nonFraction id="c141178992" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31_TypeOfArrangementAxis-InvestmentManagementAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ManagementFeeExpense" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">12.3</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c141178993" contextRef="d_2023-01-01_2023-12-31_TypeOfArrangementAxis-InvestmentManagementAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ManagementFeeExpense" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">12.8</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million for the&#160;years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em><em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>, respectively.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The incentive fee has <em style="font: inherit;">two</em> parts, as follows:</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 23pt;text-indent:23pt;">The <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> part, which is subject to the Incentive Fee Cap and Deferral Mechanism, as defined below, is calculated and payable quarterly in arrears based on the Company&#8217;s Pre-Incentive Fee Net Investment Income for the immediately preceding calendar quarter. For this purpose, &#8220;Pre-Incentive Fee Net Investment Income&#8221; means interest income, dividend income and any other income (including any other fees (other than fees for providing managerial assistance), such as commitment, origination, structuring, diligence and consulting fees or other fees received from portfolio companies) accrued during the calendar quarter, minus expenses for the quarter (including the base management fee, expenses payable under the Administration Agreement (as defined below), and any interest expense and any dividends paid on any issued and outstanding preferred stock, but excluding the incentive fee). Pre-Incentive Fee Net Investment Income includes, in the case of investments with a deferred interest feature (such as original issue discount, debt instruments with PIK interest and <em style="font: inherit;">zero</em> coupon securities), accrued income the Company has <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> yet received in cash. The incentive fee with respect to the Pre-Incentive Fee Net Investment Income is <ix:nonFraction id="c141179000" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-09-30_TypeOfArrangementAxis-InvestmentManagementAgreementMember" unitRef="Pure" name="hrzn:IncentiveFeeToPreincentiveNetInvestmentIncome" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="1">20.00</ix:nonFraction>% of the amount, if any, by which the Pre-Incentive Fee Net Investment Income for the immediately preceding calendar quarter exceeds a hurdle rate of <ix:nonFraction id="c141179001" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-09-30_TypeOfArrangementAxis-InvestmentManagementAgreementMember" unitRef="Pure" name="hrzn:PreincentiveFeeNetInvestmentIncomeHurdleRate" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">1.75</ix:nonFraction>% (which is <ix:nonFraction id="c141179002" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-09-30_TypeOfArrangementAxis-InvestmentManagementAgreementMember" unitRef="Pure" name="hrzn:PreincentiveFeeNetInvestmentIncomeHurdleRateAnnualized" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">7.00</ix:nonFraction>% annualized) of the Company&#8217;s net assets at the end of the immediately preceding calendar quarter, adjusted for any share issuances or repurchases during the relevant quarter, subject to a &#8220;catch-up&#8221; provision measured as of the end of each calendar quarter. Under this provision, in any calendar quarter, the Advisor receives <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> incentive fee until the Pre-Incentive Fee Net Investment Income equals the hurdle rate of <em style="font: inherit;">1.75%,</em> but then receives, as a &#8220;catch-up,&#8221; <ix:nonFraction id="c141179005" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-09-30_TypeOfArrangementAxis-InvestmentManagementAgreementMember" unitRef="Pure" name="hrzn:PreincentiveFeeNetInvestmentIncomeCatchupPercent" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="0">100.00</ix:nonFraction>% of the Pre-Incentive Fee Net Investment Income with respect to that portion of such Pre-Incentive Fee Net Investment Income, if any, that exceeds the hurdle rate but is less than <ix:nonFraction id="c141179006" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-09-30_TypeOfArrangementAxis-InvestmentManagementAgreementMember" unitRef="Pure" name="hrzn:PreincentiveFeeNetInvestmentIncomeMaximumRateToTriggerCatchup" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="6">2.1875</ix:nonFraction>% quarterly (which is <ix:nonFraction id="c141179007" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-09-30_TypeOfArrangementAxis-InvestmentManagementAgreementMember" unitRef="Pure" name="hrzn:PreincentiveFeeNetInvestmentIncomeMaximumRateToTriggerCatchupAnnualized" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">8.75</ix:nonFraction>% annualized). The effect of this &#8220;catch-up&#8221; provision is that, if Pre-Incentive Fee Net Investment Income exceeds <em style="font: inherit;">2.1875%</em> in any calendar quarter, the Advisor will receive <em style="font: inherit;">20.00%</em> of the Pre-Incentive Fee Net Investment Income as if the hurdle rate did <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> apply.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 23pt;text-indent:21pt;">Pre-Incentive Fee Net Investment Income does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> include any realized capital gains, realized capital losses or unrealized capital appreciation or depreciation. Because of the structure of the incentive fee, it is possible that the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>pay an incentive fee in a quarter in which the Company incurs a loss. For example, if the Company receives Pre-Incentive Fee Net Investment Income in excess of the quarterly minimum hurdle rate, the Company will pay the applicable incentive fee up to the Incentive Fee Cap, defined below, even if the Company has incurred a loss in that quarter due to realized and unrealized capital losses. The Company&#8217;s net investment income used to calculate this part of the incentive fee is also included in the amount of the Company&#8217;s gross assets used to calculate the <em style="font: inherit;">2.00%</em> base management fee. These calculations are appropriately prorated for any period of less than <em style="font: inherit;">three</em>&#160;months and adjusted for any share issuances or repurchases during the current quarter.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 23pt;text-indent:21pt;">The incentive fee on Pre-Incentive Fee Net Investment Income is subject to a fee cap and deferral mechanism which is determined based upon a look-back period of up to <em style="font: inherit;">three</em>&#160;years and is expensed when incurred. For this purpose, the look-back period for the incentive fee based on Pre-Incentive Fee Net Investment Income (the &#8220;Incentive Fee Look-back Period&#8221;) includes the relevant calendar quarter and the <em style="font: inherit;">11</em> preceding full calendar quarters. Each quarterly incentive fee payable on Pre-Incentive Fee Net Investment Income is subject to a cap (the &#8220;Incentive Fee Cap&#8221;) and a deferral mechanism through which the Advisor <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>recoup a portion of such deferred incentive fees (collectively, the &#8220;Incentive Fee Cap and Deferral Mechanism&#8221;). The Incentive Fee Cap is equal to (a)&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">20.00%</em> of Cumulative Pre-Incentive Fee Net Return (as defined below) during the Incentive Fee Look-back Period less (b)&#160;cumulative incentive fees of any kind paid to the Advisor during the Incentive Fee Look-back Period. To the extent the Incentive Fee Cap is <em style="font: inherit;">zero</em> or a negative value in any calendar quarter, the Company will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> pay an incentive fee on Pre-Incentive Fee Net Investment Income to the Advisor in that quarter. To the extent that the payment of incentive fees on Pre-Incentive Fee Net Investment Income is limited by the Incentive Fee Cap, the payment of such fees will be deferred and paid in subsequent calendar quarters up to <em style="font: inherit;">three</em>&#160;years after their date of deferment, subject to certain limitations, which are set forth in the Investment Management Agreement. The Company only pays incentive fees on Pre-Incentive Fee Net Investment Income to the extent allowed by the Incentive Fee Cap and Deferral Mechanism. &#8220;Cumulative Pre-Incentive Fee Net Return&#8221; during any Incentive Fee Look-back Period means the sum of (a)&#160;Pre-Incentive Fee Net Investment Income and the base management fee for each calendar quarter during the Incentive Fee Look-back Period and (b)&#160;the sum of cumulative realized capital gains and losses, cumulative unrealized capital appreciation and cumulative unrealized capital depreciation during the applicable Incentive Fee Look-back Period.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 23pt;text-indent:21pt;">The <em style="font: inherit;">second</em> part of the incentive fee is determined and payable in arrears as of the end of each calendar&#160;year (or, upon termination of the Investment Management Agreement, as of the termination date), and equals <em style="font: inherit;">20.00%</em> of the Company&#8217;s realized capital gains, if any, on a cumulative basis from the date of the election to be a BDC through the end of each calendar&#160;year, computed net of all realized capital losses and unrealized capital depreciation on a cumulative basis through the end of such&#160;year, less all previous amounts paid in respect of the capital gain incentive fee. However, in accordance with GAAP, the Company is required to include the aggregate unrealized capital appreciation on investments in the calculation and accrue a capital gain incentive fee on a quarterly basis, as if such unrealized capital appreciation were realized, even though such unrealized capital appreciation is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> permitted to be considered in calculating the fee actually payable under the Investment Management Agreement.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">There was <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c141179024">no</span> performance based incentive fee expense&#160;for the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>. The&#160;performance based incentive fee expense was&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c141179025" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31_TypeOfArrangementAxis-InvestmentManagementAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:IncentiveFeeExpense" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.3</ix:nonFraction> million and&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c141179026" contextRef="d_2023-01-01_2023-12-31_TypeOfArrangementAxis-InvestmentManagementAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:IncentiveFeeExpense" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">3.1</ix:nonFraction> million for the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2023,</em> respectively. The incentive fee on Pre-Incentive Fee Net Investment Income was subject to the Incentive Fee Cap and Deferral Mechanism for the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em><em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>, which resulted in $<ix:nonFraction id="c141179030" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_TypeOfArrangementAxis-InvestmentManagementAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="hrzn:IncentiveFeeCapAndDeferralMechanismReductionToExpense" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">8.9</ix:nonFraction> million, $<ix:nonFraction id="c141179031" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31_TypeOfArrangementAxis-InvestmentManagementAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="hrzn:IncentiveFeeCapAndDeferralMechanismReductionToExpense" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">9.3</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c141179032" contextRef="d_2023-01-01_2023-12-31_TypeOfArrangementAxis-InvestmentManagementAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="hrzn:IncentiveFeeCapAndDeferralMechanismReductionToExpense" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">9.8</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, respectively, of reduced expense and additional net investment income. This deferral represents a contingent future liability and is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> accrued until the amount can be reasonably estimated and payment is probable. The remaining deferred amount&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be paid up to <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> years after the date of deferment.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">The Company&#8217;s Advisor agreed to waive the portion of its quarterly income incentive fee, if any, if and to the extent that, after payment of such portion, the Company&#8217;s net investment income per share for such quarter would be less than the quarterly distribution per share declared in such quarter. The income incentive fee waiver is effective commencing with the quarter ending <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2025 </em>and terminates&#160;with the quarter ending <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025.&#160;</em>During the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c141179035">no</span>&#160;income incentive fee was earned.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">There was <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c141179036"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c141180004">no</span></span> performance based incentive fee payable at <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;"><b><i>Administration Agreement</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The Company entered into an administration agreement (the &#8220;Administration Agreement&#8221;) with the Advisor to provide administrative services to the Company. For providing these services, facilities and personnel, the Company reimburses the Advisor for the Company&#8217;s allocable portion of overhead and other expenses incurred by the Advisor in performing its obligations under the Administration Agreement, including rent, the fees and expenses associated with performing compliance functions and the Company&#8217;s allocable portion of the costs of compensation and related expenses of the Company&#8217;s Chief Financial Officer and Chief Compliance Officer and their respective staffs. The administrative fee expense was $<ix:nonFraction id="c141179038" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_TypeOfArrangementAxis-AdministrationAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AdministrativeFeesExpense" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.5</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million,&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c141179039" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31_TypeOfArrangementAxis-AdministrationAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AdministrativeFeesExpense" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.7</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, and&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c141179040" contextRef="d_2023-01-01_2023-12-31_TypeOfArrangementAxis-AdministrationAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AdministrativeFeesExpense" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.7</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million&#160;for years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em><em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>, respectively. The administrative fee payable at <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> was $<ix:nonFraction id="c141179044" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_TypeOfArrangementAxis-AdministrationAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="hrzn:AdministrativeFeesPayable" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.3</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c141179045">$0.4</span> million, respectively. The administrative fee payable is&#160;included in other accrued liabilities on the Company's Statement&#160;of Assets and Liabilities.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-indent: 18pt;"><i><b>Advisory Fee Waiver</b></i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">In connection with entry into the Merger Agreement&#160;with MRCC, HMMS, Inc., a Maryland corporation and wholly owned subsidiary of the Company, Monroe Capital BDC Advisors, LLC, an investment adviser to MRCC, and the Advisor and subject to completion of the Mergers, the Advisor has agreed to waive $<ix:nonFraction id="c141179046" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_TypeOfArrangementAxis-MergerAgreementFeeWaiverMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:InvestmentCompanyContractualAndVoluntaryFeesWaived" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">4.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million of base management fees and/or incentive fees (the &#8220;Fee Waiver&#8221;) due and payable to the Advisor pursuant to the terms of the Investment Management Agreement at the rate of $<ix:nonFraction id="c141179047" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_TypeOfArrangementAxis-MergerAgreementFeeWaiverMember" unitRef="USD" name="hrzn:BaseManagementAndIncentiveFeesAmountWaivedPerQuarter" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">1.0</ix:nonFraction> million per quarter commencing at the end of the <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> full fiscal quarter following the closing of the Mergers. The Fee Waiver will be in effect until the end of the <em style="font: inherit;">fourth</em> full fiscal quarter following the closing of the Mergers and, for each applicable fiscal quarter, will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> exceed the total amount of base management fees and incentive fees earned by the Advisor during such fiscal quarter.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-indent: 18pt;"><b><i>Exemptive Relief</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The Advisor <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>provide the Company&#160;with an opportunity to co-invest with other investment vehicles managed by the&#160;Advisor, Monroe and/or their affiliates. Under the <em style="font: inherit;">1940</em> Act, absent receipt of exemptive relief from the SEC, the Company&#160;and its&#160;affiliates are precluded from co-investing in negotiated investments with other funds and accounts sponsored or managed by the&#160;Advisor, Monroe and their affiliates. Since <em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2023, </em>the Company&#160;and its&#160;Advisor have&#160;relied on exemptive relief from the SEC granted to certain affiliates of Monroe on <em style="font: inherit;"> October 15, 2014, </em>as amended on <em style="font: inherit;"> January 10, 2023. </em>The exemptive relief affords the&#160;Advisor greater flexibility to negotiate the terms of co-investments if the&#160;Board determines that it would be advantageous for the Company&#160;to co-invest with other accounts sponsored or managed by the&#160;Advisor, Monroe or their affiliates in a manner consistent with the Company's&#160;investment objectives, positions, policies, strategies and restrictions as well as regulatory requirements and other pertinent factors. On <em style="font: inherit;"> October 2, 2025, </em>Monroe and the Advisor filed a new exemptive relief application (the &#8220;New Order&#8221;) that seeks to modify the co-investment exemptive relief previously granted to Monroe on <em style="font: inherit;"> January 10, 2023. </em>There is <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> assurance that the New Order will be granted by the SEC. In the event that the SEC grants the Company&#160;the New Order, the Company&#160;shall be required to comply with all terms and conditions required therein.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:FairValueDisclosuresTextBlock" id="c3120780" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Note</b>&#160;<b><em style="font: inherit;">6.</em></b>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;<b>Fair value</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 27pt;">Prior to <em style="font: inherit;"> July 30, 2022, </em>the Board determined the fair value of the Company&#8217;s investments. Pursuant to the amended SEC Rule <em style="font: inherit;">2a</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">5</em> of the <em style="font: inherit;">1940</em> Act, on <em style="font: inherit;"> July 29, 2022, </em>the Board designated the Advisor as the Company&#8217;s &#8220;valuation designee.&#8221; The Board is responsible for oversight of the valuation designee. The valuation designee has established a Valuation Committee to determine in good faith the fair value of the Company&#8217;s investments, based on input from&#160;the Advisor&#8217;s management and personnel and independent valuation firms which are engaged at the direction of the Valuation Committee to assist in the valuation of certain portfolio investments lacking a readily available market quotation at least once during a trailing <em style="font: inherit;">twelve</em>-month period. The Valuation Committee determines fair values pursuant to a valuation policy approved by the Board and pursuant to a consistently applied valuation process. This valuation process is conducted at the end of each fiscal quarter, with at least <ix:nonFraction id="c141179070" contextRef="i_2022-06-30_MeasurementInputTypeAxis-MeasurementInputHypotheticalMarketYieldsMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentMeasurementInput" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">25</ix:nonFraction>% (based on fair value) of the Company&#8217;s valuation of portfolio companies lacking readily available market quotations subject to review by an independent valuation firm.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The Company uses fair value measurements made by the valuation designee to record fair value adjustments to certain assets and liabilities and to determine fair value disclosures. Fair value is the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date. Fair value is best determined based upon quoted market prices. However, in certain instances, there are <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> quoted market prices for certain assets or liabilities. In cases where quoted market prices are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> available, fair values are based on estimates using present value or other valuation techniques. Those techniques are significantly affected by the assumptions used, including the discount rate and estimates of future cash flows. Accordingly, the fair value estimates <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em><em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be realized in an immediate settlement of the asset or liability.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Fair value measurements focus on exit prices in an orderly transaction (that is, <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> a forced liquidation or distressed sale) between market participants at the measurement date under current market conditions. If there has been a significant decrease in the volume and level of activity for the asset or liability, a change in valuation technique or the use of multiple valuation techniques <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be appropriate. In such instances, determining the price at which willing market participants would transact at the measurement date under current market conditions depends on the facts and circumstances and requires the use of significant judgment.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <ix:exclude>
    <div class="PGFTR" style="text-align: center; width: 100%">

       <em style="font: inherit;">138</em>

      <div class="hf-cell" style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; text-align: center; font-weight: bold; margin: 0pt; width: 99.9%; display: inline-block;">

     <div class="hf-row">
      <div class="hf-cell" style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; text-align: center; font-weight: bold; margin: 0pt; width: 99.9%; display: inline-block;">
